title: 日本へ来る前に知っておきたい日本の食事のマナー 7つ
titleTranslation: 7 Japanese Dining Manners You Should Know Before Coming to Japan
summary: The article introduces seven Japanese dining etiquette points for visitors to know before eating at restaurants in Japan, covering oshibori use, the itadakimasu/gochisousama greetings, chopstick etiquette, holding bowls, keeping elbows off the table, slurping noodles and soup, and finishing everything you order.

sentences.text: この記事では和食を食べるときに知っておきたいマナーについて紹介します。

tokens.gloss: to attach (root of について 'regarding')

sentences.translation: This article introduces manners you should know when eating Japanese food.

sentences.text: マナーを守って、ユネスコの無形文化遺産になった和食を楽しんでください！

tokens.gloss: to give (respectful; used in ~てください)

sentences.translation: Please follow proper manners and enjoy washoku, which has become a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage!

sentences.text: 日本に来たら、ぜひ楽しんでほしいものが、日本の料理です。
sentences.translation: If you come to Japan, one thing we really want you to enjoy is Japanese cuisine.

sentences.text: 寿司や焼肉、ラーメン、そして日本人が家で食べる料理とよく似た食事など、日本だからこそ食べることができる味がたくさんあります。
sentences.translation: There are many flavors you can only taste in Japan, such as sushi, yakiniku, ramen, and meals similar to what Japanese people eat at home.

sentences.text: 楽しく食事をするために、食事中のマナーにも気をつけたいですね。

tokens.gloss: for the sake of, in order to
feeling, attention (as in 気をつける)

sentences.translation: To enjoy your meal, it's good to be mindful of table manners too.

sentences.text: 自分の国では大丈夫でも、日本ではしてはいけないこともあります。

tokens.gloss: to be permissible (used in negative いけない 'must not')

sentences.translation: Some things that are fine in your own country may not be acceptable in Japan.

sentences.text: この記事では日本料理の店で食べるときに「これだけは知っておいてほしい」という食事のマナーを紹介します。
sentences.translation: This article introduces the dining manners we especially want you to know when eating at a Japanese restaurant.

sentences.text: 食べるときに困らないようにチェックしておきましょう。

tokens.gloss: to be troubled, to have difficulty

sentences.translation: Let's check them so you won't be troubled when eating.

sentences.text: 1.おしぼりは手を拭くときだけ使う
sentences.translation: 1. Use the oshibori (wet towel) only to wipe your hands

sentences.text: 大体の日本のレストランでは、入るとおしぼりを出してくれます。
sentences.translation: At most Japanese restaurants, you're given an oshibori when you enter.

sentences.text: 使ったらそのまま捨てる紙のおしぼりや、繰り返し使うことができる布のおしぼりなど、店によって種類は違います。
sentences.translation: The type varies by restaurant, from disposable paper oshibori to reusable cloth oshibori.

sentences.text: そしておしぼりは「手を拭く」ためだけのものです。

tokens.gloss: for the sake of, in order to

sentences.translation: And the oshibori is only for wiping your hands.

sentences.text: とくに布のおしぼりで、顔や口、テーブルなど手以外を拭かないでくださいね。

tokens.gloss: to give (respectful; used in ~てください)

sentences.translation: Especially with cloth oshibori, please don't wipe your face, mouth, the table, or anything other than your hands.

sentences.text: 2.食べる前と食べた後に手を合わせて挨拶する
sentences.translation: 2. Put your hands together and greet before and after eating

sentences.text: 日本では食べる前と食べた後に両手を合わせ、料理に挨拶をします。
sentences.translation: In Japan, people put their hands together before and after eating to greet the food.

sentences.text: 食べる前に「いただきます」、食べた後に「ごちそうさま」と言います。

tokens.gloss: honorific suffix (as in ごちそうさま)

sentences.translation: They say "itadakimasu" before eating and "gochisousama" after eating.

sentences.text: どちらも2つの感謝（ありがとう）の意味があります。
sentences.translation: Both phrases carry two kinds of gratitude (thanks).

sentences.text: 1つは、食事に関係しているぜんぶの人への感謝です。

tokens.gloss: to exist (animate); auxiliary for ongoing action

sentences.translation: One is gratitude toward everyone involved in the meal.

sentences.text: 食材を作ってくれた人、料理を作ってくれた人など私たちが今ここで食事を食べるために関わった、ぜんぶの人への感謝です。

tokens.gloss: for the sake of, in order to

sentences.translation: It's gratitude toward everyone who was involved in us being able to eat this meal here now, such as the people who produced the ingredients and the people who cooked the food.

sentences.text: 2つ目は、食材への感謝です。
sentences.translation: The second is gratitude toward the ingredients.

sentences.text: 肉や魚を食べることは、生きていた動物たちの命をもらうということです。

tokens.gloss: to exist (animate); auxiliary for ongoing action

sentences.translation: Eating meat and fish means receiving the lives of animals that were once living.

sentences.text: 同じように野菜にも命があると考えて、ほかの命が自分が生きるためのエネルギーに変わることに感謝します。

tokens.gloss: for the sake of, in order to

sentences.translation: Likewise, thinking that vegetables also have life, we feel gratitude that other lives become the energy for our own.

sentences.text: 3.箸を正しく使う
sentences.translation: 3. Use chopsticks correctly

sentences.text: 箸は日本で食事をするときに使います。
sentences.translation: Chopsticks are used when eating meals in Japan.

sentences.text: 箸の持ち方や、食事中の使い方にはいろいろなルールがあります。
sentences.translation: There are various rules about how to hold chopsticks and how to use them during a meal.

sentences.text: これは一緒に食べている人を、嫌な気持ちにさせないためにあるルールです。

tokens.gloss: to exist (animate); auxiliary for ongoing action
for the sake of, in order to

sentences.translation: These rules exist so as not to make the people eating with you feel uncomfortable.

sentences.text: 下の「お箸の持ち方と基本的なマナー5つ」の記事を読んで、箸のマナーも確認しておきましょう。
sentences.translation: Read the article below, "5 Basic Manners and How to Hold Chopsticks," to check chopstick manners too.

sentences.text: フォークを頼んでも大丈夫？
sentences.translation: Is it okay to ask for a fork?

sentences.text: 箸で食べることがあまり上手ではない人は、フォークがあるか店の人に聞いてみてください。

tokens.gloss: to give (respectful; used in ~てください)

sentences.translation: If you're not very good at eating with chopsticks, try asking the restaurant staff if they have a fork.

sentences.text: 店によってはフォークを貸してくれるところもあります。
sentences.translation: Depending on the restaurant, some will lend you a fork.

sentences.text: 4.お茶碗は持って食べる
sentences.translation: 4. Hold your rice bowl while eating

sentences.text: 和食や定食を頼むと、多くのレストランではご飯の入った茶碗と、味噌汁が入ったお椀が出てきます。
sentences.translation: When you order washoku or a set meal, many restaurants will bring out a rice bowl with rice and a bowl with miso soup.

sentences.text: こちらは食事のとき、手で持って食べます。
sentences.translation: You hold these in your hand while eating.

sentences.text: 片手で持つことができるぐらい軽い器は持って食べます。
sentences.translation: Bowls light enough to hold in one hand should be held while eating.

sentences.text: 例えば小さい丼ぶり、小さい皿、小鉢などです。
sentences.translation: For example, small donburi bowls, small plates, and small side dishes.

sentences.text: ラーメンやうどんなどが入った大きい丼ぶりや平らな皿は持たないでください。

tokens.gloss: to give (respectful; used in ~てください)

sentences.translation: Please don't hold large donburi bowls containing ramen or udon, or flat plates.

sentences.text: 箸を持っていないほうの手で添えて食べるときれいな食べ方に見えます。

tokens.gloss: to exist (animate); auxiliary for ongoing action
to look, to appear, to be visible

sentences.translation: Supporting the bowl with the hand not holding your chopsticks makes for a neater way of eating.

sentences.text: 5.テーブルに肘をつけない
sentences.translation: 5. Don't put your elbows on the table

sentences.text: テーブルの上に肘をついて食べると、姿勢が悪くなります。

tokens.gloss: to attach (root of について 'regarding')

sentences.translation: Eating with your elbows on the table results in poor posture.

sentences.text: そして、他の人が肘をついたあなたを見ると「悪い」と思います。

tokens.gloss: to attach (root of について 'regarding')

sentences.translation: Also, other people who see you with your elbows on the table will think it looks bad.

sentences.text: 腕は持ち上げて食事をします。
sentences.translation: Keep your arms raised while eating.

sentences.text: そして、箸を持っていないほうの手はテーブルの上におくか、器に添えましょう。

tokens.gloss: to exist (animate); auxiliary for ongoing action

sentences.translation: And place the hand not holding your chopsticks on the table, or use it to support your bowl.

sentences.text: 6. 汁や麺を食べるときは音を出しても大丈夫
sentences.translation: 6. It's okay to make noise when eating soup or noodles

sentences.text: 味噌汁、ラーメン、うどん、お茶など、和食で温かい汁の料理は音を出して食べても大丈夫です。
sentences.translation: For hot soup dishes in Japanese cuisine like miso soup, ramen, udon, and tea, it's fine to make noise while eating.

sentences.text: 麺や具を食べる時は箸を使い、汁を飲むときは両手でお椀を持ってそのまま飲むことが多いです。
sentences.translation: When eating the noodles or ingredients, people use chopsticks, and when drinking the broth, they often hold the bowl with both hands and drink directly from it.

sentences.text: しかし、すべて音を出してもいいわけではありません。

tokens.gloss: reason, sense (わけではない 'it's not that...')
classical negative auxiliary (root seen in ~ません)

sentences.translation: However, it's not the case that any noise at all is acceptable.

sentences.text: 器を置くときの音や、食べたときの咀嚼音は出してはいけません。

tokens.gloss: to be permissible (used in negative いけない 'must not')
classical negative auxiliary (root seen in ~ません)

sentences.translation: You shouldn't make noise when putting down a dish, or make chewing sounds while eating.

sentences.text: 食事中に鼻をかむときも、席から離れた音が聞こえないところでしましょう。

tokens.gloss: to leave, to be away from
to be audible, to be heard

sentences.translation: If you need to blow your nose during a meal, do it away from your seat where the sound can't be heard.

sentences.text: 音を出してもいいかわからないときは、出さないで食べたほうがいいです。
sentences.translation: If you're not sure whether it's okay to make noise, it's better to eat without making any.

sentences.text: 7．食事はぜんぶ食べる
sentences.translation: 7. Eat everything you order

sentences.text: 料理は食べることができるものだけ頼みましょう。
sentences.translation: Order only dishes you're able to finish.

sentences.text: 日本では残さないで食べることが、料理を作ってくれた人や、食材にありがとうという気持ちを伝えることになります。

tokens.gloss: to leave behind, to not finish

sentences.translation: In Japan, eating without leaving anything is a way of expressing thanks to the people who cooked the food and to the ingredients.

sentences.text: アレルギーや食べることができない食材があるときは、店の人に伝えてみましょう。
sentences.translation: If you have allergies or ingredients you can't eat, try telling the restaurant staff.

sentences.text: その食べ物を料理に入れないでくれる店もあります。
sentences.translation: Some restaurants will leave that food out of the dish for you.

sentences.text: しかしお腹がいっぱいになったときなど、どうしても食べることができないときは無理に食べなくても大丈夫です。
sentences.translation: However, in situations such as when you're already full and simply can't eat any more, it's okay not to force yourself.

sentences.text: そのときは店の人に「おいしかったです」などありがとうという気持ちを伝えて店を出ましょう。
sentences.translation: In that case, tell the restaurant staff something like "It was delicious" to express your thanks before leaving.

sentences.text: まとめ
sentences.translation: Summary

sentences.text: 楽しい食事の時間なので、マナーを知らないで他の人に迷惑をかけてしまったり、注意されて嫌な気持ちになりたくないですね。
sentences.translation: Since mealtime should be enjoyable, you probably don't want to inconvenience others by not knowing the manners, or feel bad about being corrected.

sentences.text: マナーを守って、日本の食事をたくさん楽しんでください。

tokens.gloss: to give (respectful; used in ~てください)

sentences.translation: Please follow proper manners and thoroughly enjoy Japanese food.
